title: Five Hundred Coffeehouses on the Danube
grammar: Contrastive topicalization with ami X-et illeti and viszont
goal: I can describe the social and literary role of turn-of-the-century Budapest coffeehouses.
I can frame contrasting topics using ami X-et illeti ('as for X') and X viszont ('X, on the other hand').
I can distinguish between everyday hospitality vocabulary and literary café terminology.

sections.title: The Coffeehouse Republic: Nyugat & Print Culture
body: At the turn of the twentieth century, Budapest boasted more than five hundred coffeehouses. Far more than places to drink espresso, institutions like the New York, the Centrál, and the Hadik functioned as open editorial offices, heated living rooms for penniless poets, and democratic arenas of intellectual debate.

In this unit, you will explore how the literary review Nyugat (1908–1941) transformed Hungarian prose and poetry while mastering B2 contrastive topicalization (ami X-et illeti, ezzel szemben, míg ... addig, X viszont) and focus-preverb inversion.
